scope: Editorial decisions for the v9 foundation-model evaluation (handoff dated 2026-10-04): eleven further EEG foundation models, sixteen encoder checkpoints, run as frozen probes on the eight core protocols with the published LaBraM and CBraMod frozen-row recipe and only the encoder swapped, and nine of them adapted on EEGMAT with the 2026-10-01 recipe (frozen encoder with a trained head, against rank-4 LoRA). Its own manifest: it amends no earlier review and changes no released file. The new rows sit beside the core matrix in their own files; experiments.json and the protocol files keep their bytes. The website input is the release candidate. The aggregate it was built from, the twelve group summaries its figures point into, the pretraining-exposure table, the audit status and the harness validation are pinned by SHA-256 and checked, never copied; the six independent audits stay in the private run root and are bound by the hashes the release candidate, the audit status and the handoff record.

approval.basis: Owner approval on 2026-10-04: build the v9 batch locally for review before any deploy; the owner reviews screenshots first. The release candidate keeps the status it was sealed with, 'pending user approval'; this record is that approval, and the export requires both.
approval.pretrainingExposureWording: LaBraM and CBraMod, and every model whose cell the table rates not exposed, are described as not in the authors' published pretraining list (checked 2026-10-04), with the source links; never as proven free of overlap. The core release keeps its released sentence; pages add a dated note beside it.
approval.releasedFiles: Published release payloads (experiments.json, the protocol files, adaptation-update.json) are historical records and are not edited; pages carry dated notes instead.

handoff.path: research/fm_eval_v9_20261004/Foundation Model Evaluation v9 Website Handoff.md

independentAudits.note: In the private run root; they carry private storage paths. Bound by these hashes, which the release candidate, the audit status and the handoff all record; not opened here.

verification: Every {value, src} block of the release candidate re-resolves, by its JSON pointer, to the same value in the pinned file it names (a group summary, the pretraining-exposure table, or a released site file whose bytes are unchanged).
Every frozen cell and adaptation row of the release candidate equals the pinned aggregate's row of the same id, and the aggregate records every pinned input by the hash pinned here.

All six independent audits passed with no defect; the release candidate, the audit status, the aggregate and the handoff name the same audit hashes, and every evaluated checkpoint belongs to a passing group.
The harness validation reproduced the published LaBraM and CBraMod frozen rows and idle counts, and all 45 published LaBraM EEGMAT adaptation fits, before any new score.
Every figure the pages print is the one the pinned handoff states, row by row: the frozen-probe table, the idle table and the EEGMAT adaptation table.

notPublished: Per-trial predictions, per-person and per-fold metrics, features and their hashes, the channel lists and contracts of each run.

Timing, memory, hardware and software environments: measured on a shared GPU and indicative only, so the per-protocol CSVs leave scoring_seconds empty rather than put them beside the core rows' timings.

The declared sensitivity runs (REVE without per-segment mean removal, ERP-FM with an average reference and a 45 Hz low-pass, ST-EEGFormer sleep as 5 x 6 s segments): never substituted for a primary row, and published only as the row footnotes state them.
The release candidate's generated headline sentences and the handoff's prose: the pages write their own copy from the values.
The pretraining-exposure table's process history (its open items from the previous expansion round) and its overlaps outside the seven core datasets: no page uses them.
Revisions and checkpoint hashes of the three sibling masking checkpoints: the release candidate names only the paper-recommended checkpoint's revision.
Model weights, adapted weights and LoRA deltas: never kept or shared.

The aggregate, the group summaries, the audit status and the harness validation: pinned by SHA-256 and checked, never copied, because they carry private storage paths. The six independent audits, with their check names and notes, and the run's decision log stay in the private run root; the audits are bound by hash.
